label: lem: equiv Carl
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem: equiv Carl}
    $\nu \in \mathcal C_{\mathcal{S}}$ if and only if $\mathcal{S}$ is almost sparse with respect to $\nu$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
The almost sparsity of $\mathcal{S}$ clearly implies $
u \in \mathcal{C}_\mathcal{S}$. Indeed,
    \[ \sum_{\substack{P\in\mathcal{S}\ P\subseteq S}}
u(P)\leq  rac 1\eta \sum_{\substack{P\in\mathcal{S}\ P\subseteq S}}
u(E_P)= rac 1\eta \int_S\sum_{\substack{P\in\mathcal{S}\ P\subseteq S}}1_{E_P}(x) \; d
u(x)\leq  rac N\eta 
u(S).    \]
    To prove the converse, choose a Carleson constant $\Lambda$, fix $0<\eta<1$, and let $N=\lfloor\Lambda(1-\eta)^{-1}floor$. For every $S\in \mathcal{S}$, we define 
    \[ \mathcal{E}_S(x):=\{P\in \mathcal{S}\colon x\in P\subseteq S\},\qquad E_S:=\{x\in S\colon \#\mathcal{E}_S(x)\leq N\},\]
    with the convention $\mathcal E_S(x)=\emptyset$ when $x
ot \in S$. We have
     egin{align*}
        \Lambda
u(S)\geq \sum_{\substack{P\in\mathcal{S}\ P\subseteq S}}
u(P)= \int_{S} \#\mathcal{E}_S(x)\; d
u (x) \geq \int_{S \setminus E_S} 
       \#\mathcal{E}_S(x)\; d
u(x)\geq (N+1)
u(S \setminus E_S), 
    \end{align*}
Hence we have that
     \[
u(E_S)=
u(S)-
u(S \setminus E_S)\geq \Big(1- rac \Lambda {N+1}\Big)
u(S)\geq\eta
u(S).\]
    Furthermore, for every $x\in\mathfrak{X}$ it is easy to see that $\#\{S\in \mathcal{S}\colon x\in S,\#\mathcal{E}_S(x)\leq N\}\leq N$. Indeed, if it were greater than $N$, then there would exist $S_1\subsetneq\dots\subsetneq S_{N+1}\in\mathcal{S}$ distinct such that $\#\mathcal{E}_{S_j}(x)\leq N$ and $x\in S_j$ for every $j=1,\dots,N+1$. Thus we would have that $\#\mathcal{E}_{S_{N+1}}(x)\geq N+1$, a contradiction.
    Therefore,
    $$
        \sum_{S\in \mathcal{S}}1_{E_S}(x)=\#\{S\in \mathcal{S}\colon x\in E_S\}=\#\{S\in\mathcal{S}\colon x\in S,\mathcal{E}_S(x)\leq N\}\leq N.
    $$

label: prop: somma sect
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop: somma sect}
    Let $\nu\in \mathcal C_{\mathcal{S}}$ with constant at most $\Lambda$. For every $S\in\mathcal{S}$ we have
    \[
\sum_{\substack{P\in\mathcal{S}\\P\supseteq S}} \frac{1}{\nu(P)} \leq \frac{\Lambda^2}{\nu(S)}.
    \]
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Since $\mathcal{S}$ is nested, we have that the family of $P\in\mathcal{S}$ that contain a fixed $S\in\mathcal{S}$ is an ordered nested sequence $S=P_0\subsetneq P_1\subsetneq\dots\subsetneq P_K\subsetneq\dots$. For simplicity, we set 
    \[\Sigma_K=\sum_{\ell=0}^K
u(P_\ell),\qquad K\in\mathbb N.\]
    For $K\in\mathbb N$, since $
u \in\mathcal C_{\mathcal{S}}$, we have that $\Sigma_K\leq \Lambda(\Sigma_K-\Sigma_{K-1})$. Hence we get $\Sigma_{K-1}\leq (1-\Lambda^{-1})\Sigma_K$ and iterating
    one has
    \[
u(P_K)=\Sigma_K-\Sigma_{K-1}\geq  rac 1{\Lambda}\Sigma_K\geq  rac 1{\Lambda}\Big(1- rac 1{\Lambda}\Big)^{-K}
u(S). \]
    Finally we conclude by
    \[\sum_{\ell=0}^{\infty} rac 1{
u(P_\ell)}\leq  rac \Lambda{
u(S)}\sum_{\ell=0}^{\infty}\Big(1- rac 1{\Lambda}\Big)^\ell= rac {\Lambda^2}{
u(S)}.\]

label: lem:CET
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:CET}
    Let $
u\in\mathcal C_{\mathcal{S}}$ and $\Lambda>1$ be such that $\mathcal{S}$ is $\Lambda$-Carleson in $(\mathfrak{G},
u)$. For any measurable $f\geq 0$ and $S\in\mathcal{S}$, we have
    \[\sum_{\substack{P\in\mathcal{S}\P\subseteq S}}\int_P f(x)d
u(x)\leq \Lambda\int_S \mathcal M_\mathcal{S}(f1_S)(x)d
u(x).\]
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $f\geq0$ and $S\in\mathcal{S}$. By the layer-cake formula,
\[
\sum_{\substack{P\in\mathcal{S}\\P\subseteq S}}\int_P f(x)d\nu(x)
=
\sum_{\substack{P\in\mathcal{S}\\P\subseteq S}}\nu(P)\langle f\rangle_P=
\int_0^\infty
\sum_{\substack{P\in\mathcal{S},\ P\subseteq S\\\langle f\rangle_P>\lambda}}
\nu(P)\,d\lambda.
\]
For $\lambda>0$, set
\[E_\lambda=\{x\in S:\mathcal M_{\mathcal{S}}(f1_S)(x)>\lambda\}.\]
Whenever $P\subseteq S$ and $\langle f\rangle_P>\lambda$, we have $P\subseteq E_\lambda$. Since $\mathcal{S}$ is $\Lambda$-Carleson,
\[\sum_{\substack{P\in\mathcal{S},\ P\subseteq S\\\langle f\rangle_P>\lambda}}
\nu(P)
\leq
\sum_{\substack{P\in\mathcal{S}\\P\subseteq E_\lambda}}\nu(P)
\leq
\Lambda\nu(E_\lambda).\]
Therefore,
\[
\sum_{\substack{P\in\mathcal{S}\\P\subseteq S}}\int_P f(x)d\nu(x)
\leq
\Lambda\int_0^\infty\nu(E_\lambda)\,d\lambda=
\Lambda\int_S \mathcal M_{\mathcal{S}}(f1_S)(x)d\nu(x).
\]

label: prop: infCarl
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop: infCarl}
    Let $\nu\in\mathcal C_\mathcal{S}$. We have that $\omega\in A_{\infty}^{\mathcal{S}}$ if and only if $\omega d\nu\in\mathcal C_\mathcal{S}$.
head: environment

label: eq: inf
title: Proof
body_md:
Assume that $\omega\in A_\infty^\mathcal{S}$. Then applying Lemma \ref{lem:CET} with $f=\omega$, one gets
\begin{equation}\label{eq: inf}
    \sum_{\substack{P\in\mathcal{S}\\P\subseteq S}}\omega(P)\leq \Lambda\int_S\mathcal M_\mathcal{S}(\omega 1_S)(x)d\nu(x)\leq \Lambda[\omega]_{\infty,\mathcal{S}}\omega(S),
\end{equation}
so that $\omega\nu\in\mathcal C_\mathcal{S}$. On the other hand, assume $\omega\nu\in\mathcal C_\mathcal{S}$ with constant $\Lambda'$. For $S\in\mathcal{S}$ and $x\in\mathfrak{X}$ we have that 
\[\int_S \mathcal M_\mathcal{S}(\omega 1_S)(x)d\nu(x)\leq \sum_{\substack{P\in\mathcal{S}\\P\subseteq S}}\omega(P)\leq\Lambda'\omega(S),\]
which proves that $\omega\in A_\infty^\mathcal{S}$.

label: prop:weightsparsop
title: Proposition
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Take $f\in L^1(\omega)$ normalized. By the following classical characterization of the $L^{1,\infty}$ norm, it is sufficient to prove that 
    \[\|\mathcal A_{\mathcal{S}}f\|_{L^{1,\infty}(\omega)}\approx \sup_{\substack{E\subseteq \mathfrak{G}\\0<\omega(E)<\infty}}\inf_{\substack{E'\subseteq E\\ \omega(E')\geq \frac 12 \omega(E)}}\langle \mathcal A_{\mathcal{S}}f,\omega 1_{E'}\rangle \lesssim [\omega]_{1,\mathcal{S}}(\log[\omega]_{\infty,\mathcal{S}}+1).\]
    Let $E\subseteq \mathfrak{G}$ be such that $0<\omega(E)<\infty$ and set $\gamma=2[\omega]_{1,\mathcal{S}}\omega(E)^{-1}$. We set $E'=\{x\in E\colon \mathcal M_{\mathcal{S}}f(x)\leq \gamma\}$. By the fact that $\|\mathcal M_{\mathcal{S}}f\|_{L^{1,\infty}(\omega)}\leq[\omega]_{1,\mathcal{S}}\|f\|_{L^1(\omega)}$, we have that $\omega(E')\geq \frac 12\omega(E)$. Clearly, it is sufficient to consider the averages of $f$ on sets of the family $\mathcal{S}_+=\{S\in\mathcal{S}\colon \langle{f}\rangle_{S}\leq \gamma\}$, otherwise they do not intersect $E'$. For each $\lambda\in (0,1)$, let $\mathcal{S}_\lambda=\{S\in \mathcal{S}_+\colon \omega(E'\cap S)>\lambda\omega(S)\}$ and $\mathcal{S}_\lambda^*$ be the subfamily of $\mathcal{S}_\lambda$ made with the maximal sets with respect to inclusion. We have 
    \[\sum_{S\in\mathcal{S}_+}\langle{f}\rangle_{S}\langle{\omega 1_{E'}}\rangle_{S}\nu(S)=\sum_{S\in\mathcal{S}_+}\langle{f}\rangle_{S}\omega(S)\int_0^{\frac{\omega(E'\cap S)}{\omega(S)}}d\lambda=\int_0^1\sum_{S_0\in\mathcal{S}_\lambda^*}\sum_{\substack{S\in\mathcal{S}_\lambda\\S\subseteq S_0}}\langle{f}\rangle_{S} \omega(S)d\lambda.\]
    Now fix $\lambda\in (0,1)$ and $S_0\in\mathcal{S}_\lambda^*$, by Hölder inequality for a certain $r>1$ and~\eqref{eq: inf}, we have
    \[ \sum_{\substack{S\in\mathcal{S}_\lambda\\S\subseteq S_0}} \langle{f}\rangle_{S} \omega(S)
    \leq
    \Bigg( \sum_{\substack{S\in\mathcal{S}_\lambda\\S\subseteq S_0}} \langle{f}\rangle_{S}^r \omega(S)\Bigg)^{\frac 1r} \Bigg(\sum_{\substack{S\in\mathcal{S}_\lambda\\S\subseteq S_0}} \omega(S)\Bigg)^{\frac 1{r'}}
    \lesssim [\omega]_{\infty,\mathcal{S}}^{\frac 1{r'}}\omega(S_0)^{\frac 1{r'}}\Bigg(\sum_{\substack{S\in\mathcal{S}_\lambda\\S\subseteq S_0}} \langle{f}\rangle_{S}^r \omega(S)\Bigg)^{\frac 1r} .\]
    Let $C\in (1,2)$ we decompose 
    \[ \mathcal{S}_\lambda=\bigsqcup_{k=0}^{\infty}\mathcal E_k,\qquad \mathcal E_k:=\{S\in\mathcal{S}_\lambda\colon C^{-(k+1)}\gamma<\langle{f}\rangle_{S}\leq C^{-k}\gamma\}. \]
    Let $N\in\mathbb N$ be as in Lemma~\ref{lem: equiv Carl} for $\eta=1/2$. For each $S\in\mathcal E_k$, we consider 
    \[F_N(S)=\{x\in S\colon \#\mathcal{S}_{k,S}(x)>N\},\qquad\text{where}\qquad \mathcal{S}_{k,S}(x)=\{P\in\mathcal E_k\colon x\in P\subseteq S \}.\]
    Clearly, we have that $F_N(S)$ is a union of sets of $\mathcal E_k$. 
    We set
    \[ E(S)=S\setminus\bigcup_{P\in\mathcal F_N(S)}P,\qquad\text{where}\qquad\mathcal F_N(S)=\{P\in\mathcal E_k\colon P\subseteq F_N(S)\text{ maximal}\}.\]
    By using the fact that $\nu(F_N(S))\leq \frac 12\nu(S)$ (similarly to proof of Lemma~\ref{lem: equiv Carl}), we have
    \[\sum_{P\in\mathcal F_N(S)}\int_Pf(x)d\nu(x)\leq C^{-k}\gamma \sum_{P\in\mathcal F_N(S)}\nu(P)\leq \frac 12C^{-k}\gamma \nu(S)\leq  \frac 12C \int_S f(x)d\nu(x),
    \]
    so that, by $C<2$
    \[\int_Sf(x)d\nu(x)\lesssim \int_{E(S)}f(x)d\nu(x). \]
    Furthermore, we have that the family $\{E(S)\}_{S\in\mathcal E_k}$ is pairwise almost disjoint. Indeed, for each $x\in E$, if $\#\{S\in\mathcal E_k\colon x\in E(S)\}>N$, then we have a contradiction of the definition of $\mathcal{F}_N(S)$. We now use all these elements to show that
    \begin{align*}
        \sum_{\substack{S\in\mathcal{S}_\lambda\\S\subseteq S_0}}\langle{f}\rangle_{S}\omega(S)\lesssim &[\omega]_{\infty,\mathcal{S}}^{\frac 1{r'}}\omega(S_0)^{\frac 1{r'}}\Bigg(\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\sum_{\substack{S\in\mathcal E_k\\S\subseteq S_0}} \langle{f}\rangle_{S}^r \omega(S)\Bigg)^{\frac 1r}\\
        \leq &\gamma^{\frac 1{r'}}[\omega]_{\infty,\mathcal{S}}^{\frac 1{r'}}\omega(S_0)^{\frac 1{r'}}\Bigg(\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}C^{-k(r-1)} \sum_{\substack{S\in\mathcal E_k\\S\subseteq S_0}} \langle{f}\rangle_{S} \omega(S)\Bigg)^{\frac 1r}\\
        \lesssim&\gamma^{\frac 1{r'}}[\omega]_{\infty,\mathcal{S}}^{\frac 1{r'}}\omega(S_0)^{\frac 1{r'}}\Bigg(\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}C^{-k(r-1)} \sum_{\substack{S\in\mathcal E_k\\S\subseteq S_0}} \int_{E(S)}f(x)\mathcal M_{\mathcal{S}}(\omega 1_{S_0})(x)d\nu(x)\Bigg)^{\frac 1r}\\
        \lesssim&r'\gamma ^{\frac 1{r'}}[\omega]_{\infty,\mathcal{S}}^{\frac 1{r'}}\omega(S_0)^{\frac 1{r'}}\Bigg(\int_{S_0}f(x)\mathcal M_{\mathcal{S}}(\omega 1_{S_0})(x)d\nu(x)\Bigg)^{\frac 1r},
    \end{align*}
    where we used that $(1-C^{1-r})^{-\frac 1r}\approx r'$ and that the $\{E(S)\}_{S\in\mathcal E_k}$ are pairwise almost disjoint. In particular, we stress that the constant arising in the control of the sum of $1_{E(S)}$, $S\in\mathcal E_k$, does not depend on the measure $\omega$, but on the geometry of $\mathcal{S}$. Now we conclude by passing to the sum over all $S_0\in \mathcal{S}_\lambda^*$, and by Hölder, we control
     \begin{align*}
         \langle \mathcal A_{\mathcal{S}}f,\omega 1_{E'}\rangle\lesssim&r'\gamma ^{\frac 1{r'}}[\omega]_{\infty,\mathcal{S}}^{\frac 1{r'}}\int_0^1
        \Bigg( \sum_{S_0\in\mathcal{S}_\lambda^*}\omega(S_0)\Bigg)^{\frac 1{r'}}\Bigg(\sum_{S_0\in\mathcal{S}_\lambda^*}\int_{S_0}f(x)\mathcal M_{\mathcal{S}}(\omega 1_{S_0})(x)d\nu(x)\Bigg)^{\frac 1r}d\lambda\\
        \leq&r'\gamma ^{\frac 1{r'}}[\omega]_{\infty,\mathcal{S}}^{\frac 1{r'}}
        \|f\|^{\frac 1r}_{L^1(\mathcal M_{\mathcal{S}}\omega)} \int_0^1 \lambda^{-\frac 1{r'}} \Bigg(\sum_{S_0\in\mathcal{S}_\lambda^*}\omega(E'\cap S_0)\Bigg)^{\frac 1{r'}}d\lambda\\
        \leq&rr'\gamma ^{\frac 1{r'}}[\omega]_{\infty,\mathcal{S}}^{\frac 1{r'}}\omega(E)^\frac{1}{r'}\|f\|^{\frac 1r}_{L^1(\mathcal M_{\mathcal{S}}\omega)}
        \leq 2^{\frac 1{r'}} rr'[\omega]_{\infty,\mathcal{S}}^{\frac 1{r'}}[\omega]_{1,\mathcal{S}}.
    \end{align*}
    We conclude by taking $r'=\log[\omega]_{\infty,\mathcal{S}}+2$.

    For the converse implication, assume first that $1<p<\infty$ and fix $S\in\mathcal{S}$. By testing the weak-type estimate with $f=\omega^{-\frac1{p-1}}1_S$, we obtain
\[
\left\langle\omega^{-\frac1{p-1}}\right\rangle_S^p
\omega(S)
\leq
\|\mathcal A_\mathcal{S} f\|^p_{L^{p,\infty}(\omega)}
\lesssim
\|f\|_{L^p(\omega)}^p
=
\left\langle\omega^{-\frac1{p-1}}\right\rangle_S \nu(S).
\]
Hence $\langle\omega\rangle_S
\left\langle\omega^{-\frac1{p-1}}\right\rangle_S^{p-1}
\lesssim1$, uniformly in $S\in\mathcal{S}$, and therefore $\omega\in A_p^\mathcal{S}$.
For $p=1$, fix $S\in\mathcal{S}$ and $x\in S$, and test the weak-type estimate with $f=\delta_x\nu(x)^{-1}$. Since $\mathcal A_\mathcal{S} f\geq\nu(S)^{-1}1_S$ and
$\|f\|_{L^1(\omega)}=\omega(x)$, we obtain
$\langle{\omega}\rangle_{S}\lesssim\omega(x)$. Taking the supremum of $\omega(x)^{-1}$ over $x\in S$ gives
$\langle{\omega}\rangle_{S}\|\omega^{-1}1_S\|_\infty\lesssim 1$,
and hence $\omega\in A_1^\mathcal{S}$.

label: prop: 2pesi
title: Proposition
head: environment

title: Remark
body_md:
We first recall that, in the continuous setting of the upper half-plane, the positive Bergman projector is obtained by replacing the Bergman kernel with its absolute value. Although the kernel exhibits oscillatory behaviour, it is complex-valued, and its modulus satisfies precise lower estimates. The situation is substantially different in our setting. Indeed, $K_\alpha$ is real-valued and oscillatory, and therefore its changes of sign force it towards zero. Since the underlying space is discrete, the kernel need not actually vanish, but its absolute value may nevertheless become arbitrarily small. As a consequence, $|K_\alpha|$ does not satisfy meaningful lower estimates of the desired type, and one is naturally led to replace it with a larger positive kernel.
Furthermore, the cancellation properties of $K_\alpha$ are encoded in each kernel $K_{Q,\alpha}$, $Q\in\mathcal{T}$, considered as a whole, rather than in the individual components $\langle f,h_Q^j\rangle h_Q^j$, whose number within a given cube $Q$ may be arbitrarily large. Taking the absolute value after summing over $j$, rather than term by term, therefore avoids introducing a dependence on the number of elements associated with $Q$. This is precisely what allows $\mathcal{P}^+$ to enjoy the correct size and to recover the upper estimates satisfied by $\mathcal{P}$. The distinction becomes essential when the branching function $q$ is unbounded.

title: Proof
body_md:
We prove that $K_{\mathcal{P}_m}^+$ satisfies~\eqref{eq: cond K+}. Take $x,y\in\mathfrak{X}$ and observe that $\Psi(x^{(n)},x^{(n-1)},y)=0$ whenever $1\leq n< |x|-|x\wedge y|$, by the definition of $\Psi$. Hence
        \[K_{\mathcal{P}_m}^+(x,y)=\frac{|\Psi(x\wedge y,x^{|x|-|x\wedge y|-1)},y)|}{S_{|x\wedge y|+1}}+\sum_{n=|x|-|x\wedge y|+1}^{\infty}\frac{|\Psi(x^{(n)},x^{(n-1)},y)|}{S_{|x|-n+1}}.\]
        Note that the first term vanishes whenever $x\wedge y\in\{x,y\}$, and is otherwise controlled from above and below by $m\sigma(U_{x\wedge y})$, by~\eqref{eq: def Psi} and~\eqref{eq: sect ms}. We wrote it with a small abuse of notation in the case $x=x\wedge y$. Each of the terms of the series can be controlled by the inverse of the measure of the respective sector, always by~\eqref{eq: sect ms}, yielding
        \begin{align*}
        K_{\mathcal{P}_m}^+(x,y)& \lesssim \frac{1}{m\sigma(U_{x\wedge y})}1_{x\wedge y \in \{x,y\}}(x,y)+\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\frac{1}{m\sigma(T_{x\wedge y}^{(k)})} \\
        & \approx \frac{1}{m\sigma(U_{x\wedge y})}1_{x\wedge y \in \{x,y\}}(x,y)+\frac{1}{m\sigma(T_{x\wedge y})},
        \end{align*}
        by Proposition~\ref{prop: somma sect}. If the measure $m$ satisfies~\eqref{eq: ipo Km+}, then we can also get the estimate from below for $K_{\mathcal{P}_m}^+$, by the fact that, for $n>|x\wedge y|-|x|$,
        \[\frac{|\Psi(x^{(n)},x^{(n-1)},y)|}{S_{|x|-n+1}}=\frac 1{S_{|x|-n+1}}\Bigg|\frac 1{m(x^{(n-1)})}-\frac 1{m(x^{(n)})}\Bigg| \gtrsim \frac 1{m(x^{(n-1)})S_{|x|-n+1}}=\frac 1{m\sigma(T_x^{(n-1)})}. \]

title: Example
body_md:
Let $\mathfrak{X}$ be a horocyclic tree with $q(n)\to\infty$ as $n\to\infty$ endowed with the horocyclic measure $\mu_\alpha$, $\alpha>1$, introduced in~\eqref{eq: def mu}.
Using that $q\geq2$, it is possible to
consider a family $\left\{ R_{n}\right\} _{n=0}^{\infty}\subseteq\mathcal{T}$
of sectors such that $R_n=T_{x_n}$ with $|x_n|=n+1$ and $R_{n+1}^{(2)}=R_n^{(1)}\neq R_{n-1}$. Observe that the members of the family are pairwise disjoint by construction.
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item We consider the weight
\begin{equation*}
\omega=1+\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}(q(n)^\alpha-1) 1_{R_{n}}.
\end{equation*}
    By direct computation we have 
    \[\langle{\omega}\rangle_{\dot R_n^{(1)}}\langle{\omega^{-\frac 1{p-1}}}\rangle_{\dot R_n^{(1)}}^{p-1}\geq\Big(1-\frac 1{q(n)}+q(n)^{\alpha-1}\Big)\langle{\omega^{-\frac 1{p-1}}}\rangle_{\dot R_n^{(1)}}^{p-1}\gtrsim q(n)^{\alpha-1}\to\infty,\] so that $\omega\not\in B_p^\mathcal{U}$. Furthermore, $\omega\in B_p^\mathcal{T}$ since the nontrivial means on sectors are controlled by $\langle{\omega^{-\frac 1{p-1}}}\rangle_{R_n^{(1)}}\leq 1$ and by \eqref{eq: mu set}
    \[\langle{\omega}\rangle_{R_n^{(1)}}\leq 1+\sum_{m=n}^{\infty}\frac{\mu_\alpha(R_m)q(m)^{\alpha}}{\mu_\alpha(R_n^{(1)})}\lesssim 1+\sum_{m=n}^{\infty}\prod_{j=n}^{m-1}q(j)^{-\alpha} 
    \lesssim \sum_{m=n}^{\infty}2^{\alpha(n-m)}\lesssim 1.\]
    \item We consider the weight
    \[\omega=1+\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}(q(n)q(n+1)^{\alpha-1}-1)1_{\dot R_n}.\]
    Again, by direct computation, we can show that 
    \[\langle{\omega}\rangle_{R_n}\langle{\omega^{-\frac 1{p-1}}}\rangle_{R_n}^{p-1}\geq\frac{\omega(\dot R_n)}{\mu_\alpha(R_n)}\langle{\omega^{-\frac 1{p-1}}}\rangle_{R_n}^{p-1}=q(n)q(n+1)^{\alpha-1}\frac{\mu_\alpha(\dot R_n)}{\mu_\alpha(R_n)}\langle{\omega^{-\frac 1{p-1}}}\rangle_{R_n}^{p-1}\gtrsim q(n),\] 
    and so $\omega\not\in B_p^\mathcal{T}$. On the other hand, the weight is built in a way that $\omega\in B_p^\mathcal{U}$. Indeed, all the $U\in\mathcal{U}$ on which $\omega$ is not constant are the predecessors of $R_n$'s, where $\omega\geq 1$ and, since $q(m)q(m+1)^{\alpha-1}\mu_\alpha(\dot R_m)\approx \mu_\alpha(\dot R_{m-1})$, we get
    \[\langle{\omega}\rangle_{\dot R_n^{(1)}}\leq 1+\sum_{m=n}^{\infty}\frac{\omega(\dot R_m)}{\mu_\alpha(\dot R_n^{(1)})}=1+\sum_{m=n}^{\infty}\frac{\mu_\alpha(\dot R_{m-1})}{\mu_\alpha(\dot R_{n-1})}\lesssim 1,\]
    as in the previous example.
    \end{enumerate}

title: Theorem
body_md: For every $p\in (1,\infty)$, we have $\widetilde{{B}_p}\subsetneq B_p^\mathcal{Q}$ whenever $q$ is unbounded.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $\omega\in\widetilde{{B}_p}$. Taking $Q=R$ in the definition of $[\omega]_{\widetilde{{B}_p}}$, we immediately have $[\omega]_{p,\mathcal{T}}\leq[\omega]_{\widetilde{{B}_p}}$.
It remains to control the characteristic associated with $\mathcal{U}$. Fix $x\in\mathfrak{X}$. We have
\[\langle{\omega}\rangle_{U_x}=\sum_{y\in s(x)}\langle{\omega}\rangle_{T_y}\frac{\nu(T_y)}{\nu(U_x)}\leq \max_{y\in s(x)}\langle{\omega}\rangle_{T_y}.\]
Similarly, 
\[\langle{\omega^{-\frac 1{p-1}}}\rangle_{U_x}\leq \max_{z\in s(x)}\langle{\omega^{-\frac 1{p-1}}}\rangle_{T_z},\]
so that
\[\langle{\omega}\rangle_{U_x}\langle{\omega^{-\frac 1{p-1}}}\rangle_{U_x}^{p-1}\leq \max_{y,z\in s(x)}\langle{\omega}\rangle_{T_y} \langle{\omega^{-\frac 1{p-1}}}\rangle_{T_z}^{p-1}\leq [\omega]_{\widetilde{{B}_p}}.\]

We now build an example to show that the containment is proper.
Consider a horocyclic tree such that $\|q\|_\infty=\infty$ and assume $\nu\in \mathcal C_\mathcal{Q}$ to be horocyclic. Let $\{ Q_{n}\} _{n\in\mathbb{N}},\{ R_{n}\}_{n=1}^{\infty}\subseteq\mathcal{T}$ such that $Q_{n+1}^{(2)}=R_{n+1}^{(2)}$ and $Q_{n+1}^{(1)}\neq R_{n+1}^{(1)}=Q_n$. Observe that the family $\{ R_{n}\}_{n=1}^{\infty}$ is pairwise disjoint by construction. Let $x_n\in \mathfrak{X}$ be such that $Q_n=T_{x_n}$. We choose the family in such a way that $\sup_{n\in\mathbb{N}}q(x_n)=+\infty$. We consider the weight
\[\omega =1+\sum_{n\in\mathbb N}(q(x_n)^{\frac 12}-1)1_{R_{n+1}}.\]
Observe that $\omega\not\in \widetilde{{B}_p}$. Indeed,
\[[\omega]_{\widetilde{{B}_p}}\geq
\sup_{n\in\mathbb{N}}\Bigg[\langle{\omega}\rangle_{R_{n+1}}\sup_{\substack{Q\in\mathcal{T}\\Q^{(1)}=Q_n}}\langle{\omega^{-\frac 1{p-1}}}\rangle_{Q}\Bigg]\gtrsim \sup_{n\in\mathbb{N}}\langle{\omega}\rangle_{R_{n+1}}=\sup_{n\in\mathbb{N}} q(x_n)^{\frac 12}=+\infty. \]
On the other hand, by the fact that $\nu$ is horocyclic, we have $q(x_n)\nu(R_{n+1})\leq\nu(Q_n)$. Hence, $\omega(R_{n+1})=q(x_n)^{\frac 12}\nu(R_{n+1})\leq \nu(Q_n)$ so that we can easily conclude that $\langle{\omega}\rangle_{Q_n}\lesssim 1$. Furthermore, for $m\geq n$, $\omega(Q_m)\leq q(x_{m-1})^{\frac 12}\nu(R_m)\leq q(x_{m-1})^{-\frac 12} \nu(Q_{m-1})$ and, by iteration, we have
\[\langle{\omega}\rangle_{Q_n^{(1)}}\leq  1+\frac{1}{\nu(Q_n^{(1)})}\sum_{m=n}^{\infty}\frac{\nu(Q_{m-1})}{q(x_{m-1})^{\frac 12}}\leq 1+\sum_{m=n}^{\infty}\frac{1}{q(x_{m-1})^{\frac 12}}\prod_{j=n}^{m-1} \frac 1{q(x_{j-1})}\lesssim 1,\]
by the fact that $q\geq 2$.
Using that $\omega\geq 1$ everywhere and that it is constant on all the other sectors, we conclude that $\omega\in B_p^\mathcal{T}$. Similarly, one proves that $\omega\in B_p^\mathcal{U}$.
